features.title: Game model and map
criteria: Loads data/maps/bprd-hq.json and data/maps/azuchi-castle.json into a graph with symmetric adjacency and zones per space
Legal movement: up to N spaces, passes through own fighters, does not pass through rivals unless an effect allows it (Winged Frenzy), ends on an empty space
Attack reach: melee = adjacent; range = adjacent or sharing at least one zone
State: fighters (hero and sidekicks) with life, space and owner; deck, hand, discard per player; remaining actions; whose turn it is
Exhaustion: drawing with an empty deck deals 2 damage to each own fighter
End of turn: discard down to 7 cards in hand

features.title: Combate
criteria: Card restriction by fighter (fighter name or any)
IMMEDIATELY, DURING and AFTER COMBAT windows; in the same window the defender resolves first
Feint cancels all the effects of the rival card
Combat damage = attack - defense (minimum 0); the attacker wins if it deals 1 or more combat damage, otherwise the defender wins
BOOST: Second Shot allows a boost during combat adding the boost of the discarded card
All of Medusa's cards (data/heroes/medusa.json, generated from unmatched-memory + data/heroes/overlay/medusa.json) have their effect implemented and tested

Hellboy's cards (data/heroes/hellboy.json, generated from ../unmatched-memory/data/heroes/hellboy.json + data/heroes/overlay/hellboy.json) have value, boost, type, fighter and destiny tag; their effects are resolved by the human, but the engine records life, position, discard and form (OCCULT DETECTIVE with 5 or fewer destinies in the discard, ANUNG UN RAMA with 6 or more)
features.source: Hellboy form rules: ../unmatched-hellboy-cartas/2026-10-23_2239/unmatched-hellboy-4-personajes.html, section "AHH CRAP!" (the form is recomputed from the discard; it is not permanent)

features.title: Medusa AI (heuristic)
criteria: At the start of her turn she uses her ability (1 damage to a rival in her zone) when there is a target, prioritizing killing Lobster Johnson if he has 1 life

Chooses 2 actions among maneuver, attack and scheme with a documented evaluation function (Hellboy's threat: movement 2 + possible boost, ANUNG UN RAMA +2 to the attack and free movement). She always spends her 2 actions (she cannot pass; a maneuver without moving still draws)
Kites: prefers to end out of Hellboy's attack reach on his next turn
Chooses a defense (Hiss and Slither, Feint, versatile or nothing) according to the expected value of the rival's attack and Hellboy's form
Avoids Clutching Claws and Hiss and Slither when Hellboy is a few destinies short of transforming (discarding speeds up his form), unless she wins the combat decisively
It is deterministic with a fixed seed so it can be tested
Terminal simulation: python -m sparring.sim plays Medusa(AI) games against a simple scripted Hellboy and finishes without exceptions in 100 games with different seeds

features.title: Bridge to Tabletop Simulator (not tried live)
criteria: Python client of the External Editor API: sends JSON to 127.0.0.1:39999 and listens on 127.0.0.1:39998
Only uses messageID 2 (custom message) and 3 (execute Lua). Never messageID 1 (Save & Play), which reloads the user's game

Lua snippets to: read the position of miniatures by nickname and turn it into a space (nearest snap point of the Custom_Board with board.positionToWorld), read cards from the bot seat's hand zone and from the discard by CardID, move a miniature to a space, play a card face down at a position, turn it
Does not touch the global UI (the Global's UI.setXml overwrites the savegame's roster selection): the human's button panel lives on an object of its own created by the bot with obj.UI.setXml
Tests with a fake TTS server (mock) that verify the messages sent; no test opens a connection to the real TTS
features.note: Only verified against a fake TTS server; the Lua snippets have not been run in real TTS.

features.title: Live session playable from start to finish (not tried in real TTS)
criteria: No freezing paths: every pending state (pending attack, pending_discard, owed discards, half-done bot turn) has an exit (Reveal, End action or Cancel attack) and the discard baseline is fixed before any table I/O

Retries: a table failure (settling timeout, short deal, TTS without a reply) leaves a debt (dirty/unprojected) that End action settles first; the end of the bot's turn is not skipped nor is the human's turn ended twice; the start of the bot's turn is resumable

Reconciliation is idempotent with the real table: what is already in the discard (even as a Deck) counts as moved; discard_cards and read_discard read inside Deck objects; the fake table models a Deck of 2+ cards and deck -> loose Card -> empty
bot_deck_spot is required (TypeError when building, SessionError in start()); the exhaustion of the bot's deck deals damage end to end and a short deal does not re-inflate the engine's deck
Harpies handled: the bot's defense against an attack on a Harpy is legal for a Harpy and Reveal resolves

python -m sparring.play creates the panel on an object of its own (never the Global's UI.setXml), shows the messages with broadcast and pumps poll_events into Session.handle; it survives odd events and internal errors; Ctrl+C exits cleanly (code 130) closing the listener

--read-only only sends read scripts (ReadOnlyClient wrapper + allowed labels: piece_spaces_by_guid, read_hand, count_hand, read_discard, read_face_down_cards, inspect_guids, read_health_dials, zone_overlaps) and prints a report of objects by GUID, miniatures by GUID with type and distance, life dials, hands, discards and TODOs; it warns if a discard zone overlaps a hand zone or shares cards with the hand
All new or changed builders (discard_cards, inspect_guids, broadcast) have BAD injection cases; only messageID 2 and 3; tests never touch ports 39998/39999 (connect and bind blocked in conftest)

Reply pairing: TTS does not send messageID 5; each builder script is wrapped (lua.request) with an integer id and answers through sendExternalMessage({sparring_reply=id,...}) (messageID 4) inside pcall; call_lua empties old replies before sending, drops those of another id and only attributes an error to the call if it comes back with its id; stray messageID 3 are logged and ignored

TTS reload (messageID 1): the client records it; run_loop pauses the buttons, checks all the configuration's GUIDs with inspect_guids, recreates the panel and warns; if any is missing it stops without writing to the table

HP and casualties from effects: HP events (+1/-1 for each fighter of both sides), Remove and Undo game over feed the engine (life, death, victory) and allow correcting a false victory; read_health_dials reports the dials and the session warns of discrepancies

Adopting the table: what the human moves to the bot's discard is adopted; after adopt_after consecutive table failures, or with Cancel, the engine adopts the table's hand, discard and positions; a loose bot card on the table is returned to its hand instead of repeating 'dealt 0 of 1'; deal_cards only takes objects with a CardID of the bot's deck
Ordered discard: the bot leaves each discarded card in the next slot of a grid inside its zone (skipping the draw deck) and read_discard excludes the draw decks by GUID and position

Resume: the state of Game and Session is saved as JSON atomically after each button and --resume loads it; start() with --first bot is resumable through the table debt; SessionError and connection failures come out as a clear message, not as a traceback or 'Internal error'
Pieces by GUID: piece_spaces_by_guid and move_piece with validation and BAD cases; _project checks moved; a faraway piece (off_board_dist) counts as off the board; no live path uses names
Mutants N1 (discard baseline at Reveal) and N3 (bot_stage after a retry) killed by tests; button label and messages match ('End action')

Floor markings (play mode only): draw_markings/clear_markings draw DISCARD HELLBOY, DISCARD MEDUSA, COMBAT HELLBOY and COMBAT MEDUSA with setVectorLines on the own panel and own 3DTexts, idempotent, without touching the Global or decals; --read-only does not draw them

criteria: Each message to TTS costs ~0.5 s: --timing shows per button and per bot action the messages (call_lua) and the ms; TTSClient.calls/call_seconds/trace and Session.cost_log; FakeTTS.lua_messages counts in tests

One composite script per step (lua.composite): it only composes scripts already registered by builders (validated), each in pcall, waits inside TTS for pieces and hand to settle and returns the resulting state; BAD cases (not registered, nested, request, forged header, more than 64, expect_hand)
Goal met on the fake table: Maneuver 1, End action 1, attack 3, Reveal 2, bot turn of 2 actions 3 (1 message per action); before 7, 5, 12, 17 and 43

The bot also places the human's hero (Hellboy) on his starting space during setup, in both orders; the human only places their sidekick

criteria: New panel button "Look at bot's hand" (btn_look): on only on the human's turn or during a combat, with the bot's table up to date and some card in its hand; off otherwise. It spends no action

The bot lays the cards of its hand face up in a row centered on a configurable spot (look_spot, look_step, look_rot_y in config/table.json; start-up warns if the row overlaps the panel or a combat box) and writes in the chat (ChatKind SCHEME) each card: number, title, type, value, boost and the effect text from data/heroes/<slug>.json

The human's ping (Tab) on a card of the row: onPlayerPing defined in the panel object's script (never the Global), only from the human seat and only if the card is in the row shown; it forwards it through sendExternalMessage as a look_ping event

The bot discards that card to its discard zone (next slot of the grid), returns the rest to its hand with instant moves and announces it; the engine discounts it from the hand as a forced discard and changes nothing of what it knows about the human's hand
Plan B: with a face-down card in the row, End action discards that one (0 or several face down: it moves nothing and warns); Cancel returns all to the hand without discarding
While the row is in view only ping, End action, Cancel, HP, Remove and Value are attended; the row persists in session.json (look) and --resume notes it on the panel again
Messages to TTS: show = 1 composite (row, panel and notices together), ping = 1, Cancel = 1; never messageID 1 nor Global UI
If the table does not do what the engine counted (the card is no longer there, TTS fails) the engine undoes the discard and the row stays in view; if it only takes out some cards, the row keeps those

features.title: The bot prepares the official community save itself
criteria: At start-up, fresh and --resume, if the configured discard zone GUID is not on the table the bot first adopts a Scripting zone already on the table whose position and scale match (within 1.5, any GUID or rotation), and only otherwise spawns a Scripting zone (ScriptingTrigger) with the position and scale of config/table.json (bot_discard_zone_spawn, human_discard_zone_spawn) and rotation (0, discard_zone_rot_y = 270, 0): straight, not the 269.09 / 269.43 of the hand-made zones

A discard zone that IS on the table (the hand-made 906a7a / b7a0b8 of the pre-sparring save) is only straightened to rotation (0, 270, 0); position and scale are untouched; one already straight is not touched at all

The GUID TTS gives a created zone is used for the rest of the session and kept in the session file (zones_live): on --resume at once if it changed (the rest of the file is rewritten as loaded), on a fresh start with the game's first save, so a game not begun never looks resumable; a zone left by an interrupted start is adopted by position; config/table.json is never rewritten; --resume looks for the saved GUID first, then the configured one, and creates a new zone only if neither is on the table; the table identity (config hash, fingerprint) keeps the configured GUIDs, so saves of the old table still resume
bot_discard_bounds says rotY 270 and matches the zone as created (test); the discard grid keeps exactly the same slots and all of them fit inside the zone; start-up layout warnings stay empty
The chat and console say, in es and en (i18n), which zones were created or straightened

On a fresh start only (never --resume), the objects of remove_table (GUID -> expected TTS name: decks addeca and cb6cbc, d20 65be8d, Dice Cannon 5085eb, Digital_Clocks 6126d5 and 790396; on any table, the pre-sparring one included) are DESTROYED in the same single TTS message as the zones, but only if the object is of the expected kind, lies inside remove_table_limits (|x| <= 26, |z| <= 36) and is neither an adopted zone nor a GUID the bot uses; anything failing a check is left alone and reported in the chat; absent ones are skipped; never by area or type alone; the hand cards counters d26d8c / 5c7e75, the hand and scripting zones, the fog of war trigger and the board 45c723 are never in the list (tests); each removal is reported in the chat (es and en)
Only messageID 2 and 3 of the external API are used, the Global UI is never touched; a configuration without the new keys behaves exactly as before
Verified live by Iván on the official save (docs/live-checklist.md, section Official save set-up)
verify_live: TTS keeps the scale given to spawnObject for a ScriptingTrigger (the script also calls setScale) and returns its GUID at once (no_guid is reported if not)
The created zones are the same size and place as the hand-made ones: the white floor rectangles match and the discard grid fills the bot zone
The locked Dice Cannon (5085eb) is destroyed by destruct() like the other objects, and the two clocks (6126d5, 790396) and the decks disappear; the two hand cards counters and every zone stay

The type guard: TTS Lua o.name returns the save-file names (DeckCustom, Die_20, Custom_Assetbundle, Digital_Clock), not Deck or a (Clone) suffix; if not, all six are skipped with why=type and nothing is removed
A TTS reload (messageID 1) after the zones were created: they are not in the TTS save, so the bot stops with the missing-GUID message; restart it

features.title: Every map of the official save
criteria: tools/import_map.py reads the maps of the official save (read only) and, from each board's snap points and image, writes data/maps/<key>.json (spaces, adjacency from the connectors, zones, starts) and data/maps/catalog.json; on bprd-hq it finds 51 of the 52 live-verified edges and invents none, but on a sample of four other maps it got edges wrong or missed them, so every extracted map is written "verified": false

Catalog status: supported (playable and verified by a person; only bprd-hq and azuchi-castle, live-proven), unverified (14 maps that passed the automatic checks), unavailable (15 that failed them: a space with a single neighbour, a disconnected graph, a zone or start problem), excluded (6 that need tokens or doors: Helicarrier, Hell's Kitchen, Navy Pier, Sanctum Sanctorum, The Raft with a Battlefield Items bag each, Heorot with a Doors bag; no data file). The bot only plays supported maps; an unverified one is refused with a message saying it is pending the map check

tools/map_checker.py serves a localhost-only page (stdlib http.server; foreign Host / Origin and non-JSON posts refused) over the pictures in a folder outside the repo (--images or MAP_IMAGES_DIR, <imageKey>.img): the map with numbered spaces, edges, zones and starts; click two spaces to toggle an edge, tick a space's zones, set starts; Check re-runs the structural checks (symmetric, connected, a zone on every space, published space and zone counts, starts 1 and 2 distinct) and Confirm writes the map with verified true and marks it supported in the catalog, writing nothing while a check fails (tests of the logic and the server guards, not of the page); the 15 unavailable maps can be fixed and confirmed there too

The map is found on the table by its image, never by a fixed GUID: the start-up reads every loose Board (lua.list_boards, read only, messageID 3), matches the SHA-1 the image URL ends with against the catalog and uses that board's GUID in every script (lua.board_guid, Board.guid); the three locked pad boards of the save (45c723, 8315f0, 6bd0e3, one image) are ignored; bprd-hq and azuchi-castle keep their old GUIDs as the fallback

An unknown board (a map-like image not in the catalog), none at all (only the pads), an excluded, unverified or unavailable map, or two maps at once stop the start-up (exit 2) with an i18n message (es and en) that names the map and lists the supported ones
Only messageID 2 and 3 are used, never messageID 1 or the Global UI; list_boards is read only (tests)

The Restoration Games map art is not in the repository (map pictures untracked and gitignored, history not rewritten); README documents the maps, the exclusions, what is not enforced and how to launch the checker
verify_live: TTS returns type 'Board' for o.type and the image URL in getCustomObject().image of a loose Custom_Board (the script is only tested on lupa and FakeTTS)
A map taken out of its infinite bag (new GUID) is recognised and the miniatures are placed on it; the three locked pads do not get in the way
Each map confirmed in the checker looks right on the real table: edges, zones and start spaces 1 and 2; report any wrong edge with the map and the space ids
The orange claw icons printed on some connectors (Azuchi Castle, Fayrlund Forest, Technodrome, ...): what they mean in the rules, since the bot treats those connectors as plain adjacency
The refusal messages read well on the console for an excluded map, an unverified one, an unavailable one and two maps at once
features.note: Asked by Iván on 4/11 after the bot crashed on a map picked from the official save (board.positionToWorld on nil: the board was looked up by a fixed GUID). Exclusion rule from Iván: only maps that need tokens or doors; any other special rule is listed as not enforced (the save has no rule text, so the README can only name the marks visible on the pictures). Review of 4/11: imported adjacency was wrong on every sampled map, so extracted maps need a person's confirmation in tools/map_checker.py before the bot plays them, and the map art left the repository. Branch all-maps, from official-save-setup.

features.title: Pre-game gate: check the table, clean and prepare it, start only on a button
criteria: On a fresh start (never --resume; config key pregame_gate, default true) nothing starts by itself: the bot reads the loaded table (sparring/table_reset.py, docstring = the definition of a READY TABLE) and shows only two right-panel buttons, "Clean table and prepare" (es: Limpiar mesa y preparar) while the table is not ready and "Start game" (es: Comenzar partida) once it is; the chat says what is out of place, briefly

Ready table: no remove_table leftovers (the prepare_table guard, evaluated read only); both hands empty; every card of both heroes in its deck wherever it lay (hands, discards, combat, ONGOING, look rows, loose on the table or the board; found by CardID range AND deck image); decks face down; no miniature on the board and Hellboy in his first form; life dials full and destiny 0; two-faced tokens (Hellboy ability, Abe Intuition) on their starting face; the heroes' decks, dials, pieces and tokens out of their bags; no saved game (state/session.json) for --resume; things it will not touch (other heroes' objects, a missing board, a loose object failing the name or place guard, a foreign card in a hand) are reported, not counted

Pressing the clean button, always with Medusa (bot, Green) and Hellboy (human, White) on the map the table shows: zoom copies removed, heroes unpacked from their bags, guarded leftovers destroyed, every card gathered (never destroyed) into its deck, face down and shuffled, miniatures set aside off the board, dials refilled, destiny 0, Hellboy back to his first form, tokens to their starting face, saved game deleted; no piece on the board, no hand dealt, no mulligan, no turn; the table is then read again and what is still off is named in the chat and the button stays; a second press on a ready table changes nothing

MAIN CASE, the official tournament save as it loads (tests/fixtures/official_table.json = its 170 objects): it has out the two 78-card decks, the d20, the Dice Cannon and the two clocks in the middle, no discard zones and no map (only the locked pad boards), and every hero and map inside infinite bags. The button destroys the six centre objects (GUID + expected name + inside the limits, as F20), creates the two discard zones, takes the B.P.R.D. HQ board out of its bag onto the table with the transform of config prepare_map (-0.35, 1.63, -3.18, rotY 269.99, scale 0.85, locked), takes Medusa's and Hellboy's decks, dials, pieces and tokens out of their bags, and leaves the prepared state; the hero and map bags, counters, hand zones, pad boards, fog of war trigger and everything else stay; start-up no longer stops on a table without a map (the chat says so and the button fixes it); a map already on the table is never replaced
A table showing another pair of heroes has that pair reset too but nothing is unpacked over its decks: the chat asks to put them in their bags and to press again

"Start game" re-reads the heroes and the map from the table and runs the normal start flow (deal, mulligan, placement); before the press nothing is dealt or placed; "Ready" of the setup is a different, later button (the human's confirmation after placing his pieces) and is untouched
Only messageID 2 and 3, never the Global UI; the audit scripts are read only (table_audit, deck_facing are in READ_ONLY_TAGS); texts in es and en
verify_live: lua.take_map: bag.takeObject({guid, position, rotation, smooth = false}) on the infinite 'B.P.R.D HQ' bag (ab5e89) returns the board at once (the bot reads list_boards right after) and the board keeps scale 0.85 and the lock; the bag is still full afterwards; the map lies on the pad board and the discard grid, decks and combat spots of config/table.json fall on it as in the earlier games

unpack_from_bags with outers: the infinite bag spawns its copy of the inner bag LATER, so the script takes it with takeObject's callback_function, takes the items out of the copy in the callback and sends the reply from there (the request wrapper's JSON.encode answers by request id whenever it runs; the client waits 5 s + 8 s and the script answers on its own after UNPACK_SPAWN_WAIT = 4 s with why=spawning). Check live: ONE press unpacks both heroes, the reply arrives (no TimeoutError), the emptied copy is destroyed, no loose bag copy is left on the table; if a press ends 'spawning' the copy it left is found loose by its contents and reused by the next press (no duplicates); the callback receives the spawned bag (not nil) and its getObjects() lists the items at that moment; a loose Bag is only reused if it lists every item still missing
Medusa's and Hellboy's objects unpack to their rows and deck spots on the official table (play.prepare_heroes) and nothing lands on a hand zone or on the map's spaces
TTS keeps the panel's two new buttons hidden in a game and shows them, one per row beside Mulligan and Ready, in the gate; the labels fit the column
The panel XML exists 0.5 s after create_panel: PANEL_SETTLE (0.7 s) is enough for the first set_panel of the gate to take effect
Object.is_face_down and Object.flip() on a Deck/Card: a face-up deck is turned down; the deck stays within deck_radius of its spot
The Scope(everywhere) read finds loose cards of the heroes anywhere (also on the board and under other objects) and nothing of other card games (identity check)

Hellboy's miniature goes back to state 1 with set_state and keeps its place; his ability token ends at rotZ 180 (OCCULT DETECTIVE); Abe's Intuition tokens end inactive (rotZ 0, to be confirmed with the Abe verify_live)
The o.name values of the remove_table objects (see F20) also decide what the audit reports as leftovers
table_audit counts Player[seat].getHandObjects(1) per seat; the zoom copy (SparringZoom) is destroyed by clear_markings(remove_panel=True)
After cleaning, the reading finds the table ready: nothing is left unfound because of an object type TTS reports differently

features.title: The player sets the table: Clean table, drag map and heroes, Prepare (per-map calibration)
criteria: Three gate buttons (btn_clean, btn_prep, btn_start; events clean_table, prepare_table, start_game; es/en captions): Clean table and Prepare are offered while the table is not ready, Start game only when it is; Clean table stays available on a ready table to change heroes or map

Clean table (lua.clear_setup) destroys every hero object (Deck/Card whose cards are all a hero's by CardID range AND deck image or its character card, also in a hand; loose bags that hold only hero GUIDs; loose objects inside the play area whose GUID is a hero's or whose name is a fighter's) and every Board whose image is a catalog map; never an infinite bag, the pads, zones, triggers, hand zones or anything beyond |x| 26 / |z| 36; a pile mixing hero and foreign cards is left and reported. It also creates the discard zones, removes the guarded leftovers of the official save and deletes the saved game
The real clear_setup script on the 170 objects of the official save destroys nothing (tests/test_official_table_gate.py)

Prepare (sparring/player_setup.py) reads boards, loose bags and loose decks in one message: the map by its image, each half's hero by the bag copy it holds (every GUID in it is the hero's) or by its loose deck (CardID range AND image); the bot's half is +x, the player's -x. It says 'Bot: X, Tu: Y, Mapa: Z'. A hero the bot cannot play (catalog name or unknown bag), a missing or repeated hero, two heroes on one half, the same hero on both halves, no map or an unplayable map: clear chat lines and nothing is touched

Closed bags (a copy with a GUID of its own) and opened contents both work, mixed too: the items come out of the copy the player dropped (unpack_from_bags with the copy as the bag; adopted copies are destroyed once empty); a deck counts as present only with the hero's image (heroes share CardID ranges)

Map calibration (sparring/map_setup.py, config/map_setups.json): a calibrated map is laid at its scale, position and rot_y (lua.place_map, locked) and brings its own layout slots and deck spots (bot_deck_spot / human_deck_spot are its deck slots: play.detect_board applies them, so in-game deck finding points at where the decks were laid); B.P.R.D. HQ's entry is the transform and layout verified live on 5/11. An uncalibrated map is used as it lies with the default layout of config/table.json and the chat prints the exact calibrate command

python -m sparring.calibrate --map <key> [--dry-run] reads (read-only scripts only) the board's transform and every deck, character card, dial, token and miniature of both heroes from the table arranged by hand, in the order of the layout slots, and writes that map's entry keeping the others; it names what it could not find and writes nothing then

Tested with two non-default heroes (Bigfoot vs Houdini) on another map: closed bags, opened contents, heroes on swapped halves, both on one half, uncalibrated and calibrated maps, a lost piece, a failing preparation, Medusa vs Hellboy through the old dirty-state matrix, and the calibration command
verify_live: What dragging a hero from the roster gives: a Bag copy of the inner bag whose getObjects() lists the same GUIDs as the data (d42056... for Medusa); list_bags and the match against data/tts must recognise it, and the items must come out of the copy by those GUIDs
What dragging a map gives: a Board (type Board, image of the catalog); Clean table must destroy it even locked, and place_map must scale and lock it
Objects taken out of a copy keep their GUIDs (the template is not in the world); if TTS renames one, Prepare reports it as missing and session.resolve_pieces handles the pieces it can by name
Opening a bag and spreading its contents by hand: the loose deck (31 cards, character card inside) is read as the hero by CardID range and image
clear_setup: Deck/Card getData() of a pile in a hand, held_by_color, and destruct() of a locked Board
calibrate: read_transforms returns clean rotations for decks (rx 0 / 360, rz 180) and the board's getScale().x; the bot must be closed (same listen port)
features.note: Asked by Ivan on 6/11. Replaces the single 'Clean table and prepare' button of F22 (always Medusa vs Hellboy on B.P.R.D. HQ). Branch feat/player-setup from master 5815b9b. The infinite-bag path of unpack_from_bags (outers) is no longer used by the gate.

features.title: Sinbad (Battle of Legends, Volume One, with The Porter) playable by the bot and by the human against every hero
criteria: data/heroes/overlay/sinbad.json, data/heroes/sinbad.json, data/heroes/effects/sinbad.json and data/tts/sinbad.json generated and validated (import_hero, validate_effects, import_save); the 16 titles (30 cards, sheet 176, character card 303) read from the card images; the seven VOYAGE cards carry the tag voyage and the HeroDef counter voyage counts them in the discard pile; ai_profile computed by the importer

His deck shares CardIDs 17600-17629 with the other sheet-176 decks: told apart by deck image and owner, never by a bare CardID (tests/test_hero_sinbad_data.py, tests/test_card_identity.py); no GUID of his is shared with another hero

The ability (+1 space per VOYAGE card in the discard pile for each fighter in a Maneuver) is the passive rule maneuver_move_per_counter: Game.maneuver adds it, the bot's planners and the search count it, the human gets a chat hint (tests/test_sinbad_effects.py, tests/test_sinbad_human.py)

All 16 cards on the interpreter for both seats: the seven VOYAGE attacks (value 2 plus the other VOYAGE cards in the pile; Voyage Home, the random discard, the look, 2 damage, the heal, the draw, the move), Commanding Impact, By Fortune and Fate, Momentous Shift, Regroup, Toil and Danger, Leap Away, Feint, Exploit and Riches Beyond Compare; no plugin
Sinbad against each of the 19 other heroes in both seats reaches game over on FakeTTS (passive and attacking human) and in the simulator (tests/test_sinbad_matrix.py)
